doc.title: Bley Carla — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Selling arrangements, guest conducting and commissions
summary: Big bands buy her scores, she guest-conducts in Europe, and a recent commission barely covered copying.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Do you get a lot of interest and purchases for your compositions there?

Yeah, but a lot of them are the big band. Every city, every school has a big band. And that’s how... by furnishing them with things with the exact instrumentation of the band they already have, they order it. And then sometimes a lot of people want to do Escalator Over The Hill and they just do it by buying it. But that’s not a money making thing. That’s just the cost of labor involved, it just covers the cost of the labor and the postage.
Does this also provide the opportunity for you to be a guest artist with ensembles around the country? Around the world?

Well I’ve been the guest conductor and composer with many big bands in Europe. But I think only one in the United States. Oh, two. One in Texas, one in Vermont. But Europe basically has a lot of big bands. Radio big bands, not only schools, radios, cities, god, bands all over the place. And they buy the stuff and play it.
Are you finding yourself being asked for commissions from someone like the GDR/DDR Radio Bands in Germany or any of the... is there?

GDR, no. All the other ones, yes. And let’s see. The last commission that I got was two years ago and that was for the Boys Choir big band piece. It was played in the Morris Festival and that was like 80-90 people.
And the commission just about covered the copying cost.

Yeah I have a cassette of the videotape of it. The Boys Choir was insanely great. I want to do this piece over here. I used a German boys choir and it’s sort of a little bit confusing cause it’s about people learning how to speak French. So there were so many languages going on. I want to do it with the American Boys Choir and my own big band. So when I become a billionaire I’ll do it. Just waiting.
